# Current instruction preservation trials

This frozen matrix checks current candidate instruction behavior against explicit
scope, authority and evidence requirements. It is separate from the matched
frontend quality comparison and the closed retained-baseline efficiency study.
It makes no efficiency, statistical reliability or universal compliance claim.

Each case receives the full root completion contract and its relevant private
references. Target Help metadata and completion text use the same renderer as the
candidate projector. Original source hashes and rendered instruction hashes are
recorded separately. The task receives complete synthetic facts, while the scoring
criteria remain outside its prompt. Twenty-two cases are response-only; two run
real local Node verification lifecycles with product files outside edit authority.

Freeze before any responses. One attempt per case, no automatic retry. Preserve
raw events, model usage when emitted, tool activity, before/after files and process
observations. Missing telemetry or an incomplete process observation is a failure.
Runtime model identity is unverified when the CLI does not emit it. The existing
configured host is used without model/reasoning/sandbox/approval overrides.

A completed CLI turn is not behavioral acceptance. Independent review must inspect
every response and applicable actual artifacts, including unchanged product bytes,
real endpoint results, evidence survival and owned-process cleanup. Source changes
invalidate the affected rendered input; keep old trials and record the repair.

Commands: `node scripts/adoption-behavior-trials.mjs freeze`, then `verify`, then
`run /tmp/qs-adoption-behavior-20260925`. Capture requires the existing Codex runtime
write interface, as established by the frontend pilot; isolated fixtures do not
change installed skills or real projects.
